scope: Independent review of the complete four Korean learner notebooks, four English teaching keys, Week 1 course contract, distributed data and four standalone HTML handouts. Each book passes for its defined Week 1 teaching role after the substantive rewrite and the required-assignment correction. The domestic 2027 middle-school scope, the 2026 high-school-level reference examples and the original international tasks have separate roles. The examples below use public or independently chosen data.

independence.method: I set the seven textbook questions from the sources and rejected edition before reading the rewritten student material. I reviewed the full Korean text and guides, checked named scientific facts and real data, solved fresh problems, ran the public code in separate namespaces, and deliberately tried plausible wrong methods. I neither wrote the lessons nor selected the examiner’s private answers. I furnished a separate blind response before I saw the source-grounding or final native reviewer request.

fingerprint_method: Raw notebook SHA-256 identifies the author manuscript tested. Published notebook and HTML SHA-256 identify the actual distributed bytes. The authored-cell projection retains every nbformat v4 cell in display order, removes outputs, execution_count and metadata.execution, and hashes sorted-key UTF-8 Python JSON with ensure_ascii=False and default separators. All four native learner sources matched those cells and each English guide was present in the final native teacher packet.

download.comparison: Native data URI decoded by both strict Base64 and a standard URI reader. Each byte equalled the installed executable notebook.

week01_integrated.ipynb.role: Data representation, descriptive statistics and required transfer
week01_integrated.ipynb.original: The title frames the subject as extracting an answer row. The main example alternately identifies the plant pot, the record and the plotted mark as the observational unit. Its introductory use of ID does not explain what the identifier distinguishes or why it differs from a position. The variance paragraph describes subtraction from the mean in the wrong direction. The displayed signs actually require value minus mean. The code and printed variance still agree because squaring erases that error.
week01_integrated.ipynb.changed: A real hand-written digit supplies the object, feature measurements and class. Signed deviations, observed denominators and the information lost by a projection now have worked reasons. Four required integrative problems include a hand proof and a general implementation on changed inputs.

teaching.finding: The digit example distinguishes one image, a 4×4 block's foreground-pixel count, a flattened feature index and a digit class. Fixed-order flattening preserves the 8×8 array; counting pixels within a block loses locations. The book now defines deviation as value minus mean, its descriptive variance and its standard deviation as the square root in the original unit, then separates the registered value of zero from a deliberately masked copy. A real same-coordinate/different-label collision supplies a counterexample to perfect classification with two features. The optional center derivation completes the square and explains why the cross term vanishes.

application.case: Use a class collision on genuine digits outside the worked pair, add a feature on a new matrix, and check class-wise plotting and missing named columns on a changed dataset.
application.observed: Source images 4 and 81 have true classes 4 and 7 but both map to (1,16) at the two chosen positions. Their full 64-dimensional squared distance is 2,904. In a separate fresh table, adding a coordinate eliminated four projection conflicts; it could not create a new one. In independent checks actual Matplotlib and Seaborn bars agreed under the declared group denominators, and an all-missing feature returned no mean while an observed zero contributed to its count. These finite cases support the stated impossibility and its limits. In the corrected required fourth problem the single-column hand calculation gives pair [0,1]; retaining both printed columns eliminates the conflict. Independently grouping projected feature tuples agreed with the public teacher function on 3,510 retained-column choices across 585 small binary tables, including repeated and reordered features. The reader must also explain why equality on the longer tuple implies equality on the original tuple.

week01_python_tables.ipynb.role: Python, named tabular features, descriptive statistics and graph reading
week01_python_tables.ipynb.original: The opening sends learners from reading a table cell to an answer. It introduces averaging by combining physical rods, uses vague dispersion wording, and makes the unconditional claim that a scatterplot point is one pot. This hides the distinction between each record contributing a coordinate pair and the number of distinct visible marks. The derivation of descriptive variance, explicit units and conditional observed-water mean later in the book are mathematically usable.
week01_python_tables.ipynb.changed: Genuine digit data lead the core, with new named-array, join, moment and plot work. Counterfactual examples identify which measurements were exchanged while preserving both marginal lists. The artificial CSV is separately optional and includes its measurement period and units.

teaching.finding: The opening distinguishes a machine-learning example (one digit image), a row position, its numeric class and the statistical sample used for inference. The length example gives the signs, squared units, n denominator and nonnegative square root; the optional n−1 estimator is limited to a different question. A zero observed pixel count, a zero class label and a removed measurement are separated. The scatterplot defines paired coordinates and explains overlapping marks. The synthetic plant CSV has its own optional appendix with an explicit simulated object, time period and units.

application.case: Reorder named rows and features, check different genuine digit images where two measurements are exchanged, and reconstruct the two requested graph types from independently joined measurement and target CSVs.
application.observed: The paper and executable arrays identify source index 2, feature 19, and its value 13 separately from digit label 2. In the lesson's counterfactual the digit-0 mean moves from 9 to 13/3 without changing either univariate list. In another six-image selection the same kind of exchange changed the two class means from (16,13) to (14,15), again preserving the marginals. The new CSV task yielded histogram counts [1,2,3] in both plotting systems; an omitted label stayed missing and a duplicated lookup key was rejected. The explanations apply to those selected records.

week01_axes_linear_bridge.ipynb.role: Array axes, matrix products, vector similarity and information lost in aggregation
week01_axes_linear_bridge.ipynb.original: The bridge opens with a fictional plant photography schedule and an unexplained ID. Its literal reading of X[1,0] equates the numeric count 1 with a physical leaf. An array entry is a feature measurement; the data never identify that individual leaf. The story and output names precede the actual vector/matrix argument and therefore obscure what a weighted sum retains. The later index-contraction check and cosine normalization do teach valid mathematics.
week01_axes_linear_bridge.ipynb.changed: Actual array elements are grayscale or RGB measurement codes. The revised order leads from named axes to signed linear combinations, similarity or cost decisions, and an explicit failure of temporal pooling to recover order. Direct entry defines the identifiers used there.

teaching.finding: The opening specifies two 8-bit grayscale codes and defines the image identifier separately from its array position. The input axes have names. The mean and signed difference determine different columns of the coefficient matrix; matching the input-feature index derives each output scalar and the real-vector linearity claim. A cold start at the search section defines query, candidate, ID, dot product and row normalization. The masked token mean states which axis disappears, why measured zero counts and why padding does not.

application.case: Choose an RGB channel order with a red value below blue, transpose the named inputs, and compare a query with a longer sequence having a different first token and the same pooled vector. Exercise the signed score, rounding/tie rule and a genuine zero token.
application.observed: The independently recomputed contrast was −248 even with an unsigned input array. Jointly permuting names and values preserved it. A stale label order changed the contrast while leaving the mean within floating-point precision. Valid sequence lengths 2 and 4 with different first tokens both yielded [3,1.5], preventing recovery of either requested field from the mean. The guide code preserved the requested gallery IDs under permutation and its stated tie rule. A real all-zero token counted as one; an all-padding input had an undefined mean.

week01_problem_pipeline.ipynb.role: Partially labeled supervised classification and held-out evaluation
week01_problem_pipeline.ipynb.original: The headings ask whose row, what answer line, which two points the model learned, and which three artworks go on which lines. An unknown label, a missing measured feature, an individual example, the training-derived fill value and a class centroid have different mathematical roles, but the opening directions substitute ‘known works’ and ‘learned value’ for several of these. The solution misnames a prediction-to-record permutation error as an error in which artwork was selected. The worked square distances and the warnings about validation reuse are sound.
week01_problem_pipeline.ipynb.changed: The original official CSV establishes what is known in partially labeled training. Worked examples then separate unknown class, missing measurement, imputer, class center, prediction and later evaluation. The guide supplies a numerical derivation and a three-feature application. The output-file exercise is optional.

teaching.finding: The three displayed rows and the count of 496 unidentified, two replica and two authentic paintings match the official 500-row training CSV. The text identifies the five numerical coordinates and makes clear that the source omits their physical meanings. The synthetic calculation labels its different data and policy. It derives the class center from the sum of squared deviations, interprets a two-coordinate decision boundary, and shows why a held-out evaluation can disagree with a correctly computed predicted class. Submission mechanics are an optional application after the supervised problem.

application.case: Use a new point where the nearest known individual and nearest class center disagree. Independently solve the three-feature exercise with its changed label encoding, then change a held-out label and test the file round trip with nonnumeric-looking IDs.
application.observed: On the independent numerical problem the class-center squared distances were 64 and 16, choosing the other class from the nearest training example. Replacing an evaluation label changed no fitted mean or predicted class. On the new three-feature learner task the independent class centers were [1,3,1] and [7,5,3]; its requested validation point had squared distances 17 and 9. Comparison by ID identifies V3 as the error (two of three correct). A quoted or leading-zero ID survived a physical CSV round trip and an extra CSV field failed the verifier.

official_sources.finding: The organizer lists subjects 1–4. The first period is a three-hour written exam and the second is a three-hour coding exam. International selection eligibility is separately described.

official_sources.source: Official scope linked by the Korean organizer
official_sources.finding: The organizer's published scope identifies its IOAI 2026 basis and includes practical Python, array/table work, and visualization. This four-book review covers the stated Week 1 subset.
The prior reference paper was prepared at a high-school reference level and does not provide an official answer key. It is not a released 2027 middle-school exam.
The concrete decisions about axes, joint versus marginal representations and transposition informed the independent probes.

official_sources.source: UCI Optical Recognition of Handwritten Digits
official_sources.finding: Each of 64 numeric features counts foreground pixels in a nonoverlapping 4×4 block of a 32×32 binary image.
The bundled subset has 1,797 observations, 64 features with values from 0 to 16, ten classes and an 8×8 representation.
Variance uses squared deviations and denominator N−ddof; the descriptive and inferential uses are separate.
A scatterplot pairs two variables for corresponding observations. Marginal values alone do not recover those pairings.
The Euclidean class representative is the arithmetic mean and a new observation is assigned to the closest representative under the stated classroom rule.

official_sources.source: IOAI 2025 Restroom Icon Matching, official notebook
official_sources.finding: Retrieve the opposite sign at the same restroom. The original query and candidate collections and output IDs differ from synthetic vector-scoring examples.

official_sources.source: IOAI 2025 Antique Painting Authentication, original statement and CSV
official_sources.finding: The five numeric features precede the class field. In the public training CSV I independently counted 496 unknown targets, two replicas and two authentic works and matched the three printed data records. The statement asks for use of unlabeled training records. A supervised classroom center model addresses only part of that task.
For each input audio chunk the prediction is its chronological rank. A list of chunks in chronological order encodes the inverse relation.
The original supplies 1,602 vocabulary entries and public vectors of length 2,560, without a labeled training split. It includes public games and evaluates with a hidden representation.
The bounded coordinate exercise illustrates part of the 224×224 image area budget, not the competition's model-performance objective.

course_bounds.registered_skill: On unfamiliar labeled vectors, determine whether selected features distinguish the required outcomes. Find every different-class pair with equal retained coordinates, explain the effect of another observation, and distinguish a finite collision from generalization. A separate new input checks class-center or similarity reasoning. Retrieval preserves its original candidate identifiers.
course_bounds.bound: The five class blocks total two hours. The registered homework route totals five hours within the historical five-to-seven-hour planning range. The axes bridge, extra array transformations and extended file practice have conditional routes. Foundation joins and plots carry across the alternatives. The instructional estimates have no observed completion-time data.

routes_and_verification.whole_book_execution: All 98 authored code cells across 231 learner cells completed in four initially clean IPython namespaces. I checked the actual public guide functions with independent examples after executing the student code. Worked cells, intentionally unfilled answer cells and separately supplied self-checks retain distinct purposes.
routes_and_verification.written_entry: The separate tables-paper section contains two selected-response questions and one written item. I worked the retained-axis and denominator decisions from the supplied inputs.

published_html.result: The four handouts contained all ordered student cells. Visible code matched each notebook. Saved table headers, row/column order and values matched every rich DataFrame in each HTML. All embedded PNGs matched their source bytes and authored alternative text. Every local reading link and fragment resolved. The integrated handout routes to eight distinct sections of its companion books.
published_html.download_verification: I checked the visible native named download link on every installed handout, decoded each payload using strict Base64 and a standard offline URI reader, and compared all bytes with the installed notebook. The verifier rejected a wrong suggested filename, a truncated payload and a relative file link.

mobile_figures.result: I verified checkbox and label associations and named, focusable scroll regions. Using the shipped styles I measured the ten images in compact and expanded states at 390 pixels and in desktop layout at 1280 pixels. Expanded mobile figures reached their intrinsic widths, and the scroll regions stayed inside the viewport.
mobile_figures.execution_limit: The local independent measurements use WeasyPrint and static HTML. This reviewer could not start a local Chromium singleton socket. Actual keyboard, pointer and assistive-technology interactions were unobserved here.

routes_and_verification.book_necessity: I found a distinct, assessed use for each existing book: the integrated representation problem, the foundation’s named tables and plotted data, the bridge’s linear maps and pooled information, and the pipeline’s fitted rule and held-out evaluation. The class route uses selected sections. The gaps in the rejected baseline have been addressed within these roles. A fifth Week 1 notebook is unwarranted on the reviewed evidence.
limits: This review measures the teaching material and observed software behavior. No Korean students took part. Learning, performance under supervision, contest scores, accessibility with assistive technology and actual completion times remain unmeasured.
Released notebooks, worked answers and public validation files support practice. A proctored judgment of independent student work would require collecting first answers on fresh material.

The numerical tasks cover Week 1 prerequisites. They do not demonstrate full contest-level image recognition, semi-supervised training, audio ordering, all other domestic topics or prediction for the next cohort.

revision_history.reason: The original calculation, download and browser checks passed. Reading the actual lessons and solving a changed problem exposed a reversed signed deviation, a count equated with a physical leaf, missing explanations of overlapping points, and undefined training and identifier terminology. The separate negative receipt gives cell evidence and an independent counterexample for each member.

The only request to implement the registered independent representation test appeared as “추가 문제” after three numbered problems. The classroom proof and code were sound. The handout allowed the stated core tasks to end before the substantive transfer.

I compared the new student and teacher cells directly with the first rewritten edition and the physical files. Section 8 explicitly assigns four numbered problems. Problem 4 requires the hand calculation, a general function on unfamiliar inputs, and a reason for the effect of feature addition. The teacher collects all three in the named response cell. Other sections and the three companion manuscripts retained their previously checked content.
